candidates.title: Pentagon releases UAP report
candidates.quote: On June 25th, 2021, the Pentagon released a report acknowledging the existence of objects in our sky that we cannot explain.

link.reason: Both are about the June 2021 Pentagon UAP report, the same document at the same grain.
link.difference: Gives the release date of June 25th, 2021 and frames the report as admitting there are objects nobody can explain, where Weinstein speaks of its nine dull pages and what they suggest.

candidates.title: Fravor's Tic Tac encounter
candidates.place_text: off the coast of San Diego
candidates.quote: Pilots like Commander David Fravor, who saw the famous Tic Tac in 2004 off the coast of San Diego.

link.reason: Both describe David Fravor's 2004 encounter with a UFO off San Diego during the Nimitz events. This telling calls it the Tic Tac.
link.difference: This telling names the object as the 'Tic Tac' and places it off San Diego, but it does not say the object seemed conscious or seemed to notice Fravor looking at it.

candidates.title: Air Force Project Blue Book
candidates.quote: The Air Force even established its own UFO investigation program called Operation Blue Book.

link.reason: The telling is about the Air Force's Project Blue Book (1947-1968). None of the stories covers it. The nearest is AATIP, which is a different program run by a different agency in a different period.

candidates.title: Trinity and Roswell crashes
candidates.quote: Known crashes like those at Trinity and Roswell

link.reason: The telling mentions the Trinity and Roswell crashes together as examples of known crashes. The nearest story is the 1945 Trinity crash told as the source of a larger piece, which covers only one of those crashes and makes a specific claim about the material. The telling is a wider passing reference that covers two crashes, so it is not the same story.

candidates.title: Kenneth Arnold sighting
candidates.quote: sightings like that of Kenneth Arnold

link.reason: The telling is Kenneth Arnold's 1947 sighting in the United States. None of the stories is about Arnold. The closest ones, Project Blue Book and Roswell, are a program and a crash, not this sighting.

candidates.title: 1952 Washington, D.C. sightings

link.reason: None of the stories covers the July 1952 Washington, D.C. sightings. The closest ones (Kenneth Arnold 1947, Project Blue Book) are a different sighting and a broader program.

candidates.title: CIA memo calls UFOs a national security matter
candidates.quote: This prompted a very concerned CIA to write a memo saying that the UFO phenomena was a matter of national security and could touch off mass hysteria and panic.

link.reason: The telling is about a 1952 CIA memo that called UFOs a national security matter. The closest story is the July 1952 Washington, D.C. sightings, which seem to have prompted the memo, but those sightings are a separate event and the memo is a separate document. None of the other stories, such as Blue Book or AATIP, is about this memo.

candidates.title: Robertson panel recommends downplaying UFOs
candidates.quote: A commission of academics was then formed by Caltech physicist Dr. H.P. Robertson. It suggested that the government should systematically downplay the phenomena through media, movies, and other means.

link.reason: The Robertson panel's 1953 recommendation to play down UFOs is its own event. The nearest story, the 1952 CIA memo calling UFOs a national security matter, is the document that led up to the panel, not the panel or its recommendations.

candidates.title: Condon report closes Blue Book
candidates.quote: The 1968 Condon report closed shop on Bluebook and dismissed a lot of its findings with very prosaic explanations.

link.reason: The nearest story is the Air Force's Project Blue Book program as a whole. This telling is about one specific document, the 1968 Condon report, and its role in shutting that program down. That is a distinct event at a narrower grain, not the program itself.

candidates.title: AATIP revealed by Leslie Kean
candidates.quote: That was until 2017 when a New York Times journalist named Leslie Kean revealed that the government had a UFO investigation program called AATIP that had formed in 2007 and was being run under the auspices of Bigelow Aerospace.

link.reason: Both tellings are about AATIP, the US government UFO program formed in 2007. This one describes the program by way of its 2017 New York Times disclosure rather than a separate incident inside it.
link.difference: Adds that Leslie Kean revealed the program in the New York Times in 2017 and that it ran under Bigelow Aerospace, and gives no $22 million budget.

candidates.title: Pan-STARRS discovers 'Oumuamua
candidates.quote: In 2017, the Pan-STARRS telescope in Hawaii discovered a fast-traveling object in space called Oumuamua.

link.reason: The telling is about Pan-STARRS discovering 'Oumuamua in 2017. No story in the corpus covers that object or that discovery. The nearest stories are other sightings (Nimitz, Kenneth Arnold, Washington 1952), and they are different events.

candidates.title: Loeb's artificial light-sail theory of 'Oumuamua
candidates.quote: All of the proposals that were put on the table to explain the anomalies of Oumuamua invoked a rock of a type that we've never seen before.

link.reason: The nearest story covers Pan-STARRS discovering 'Oumuamua in 2017. That is the sighting event. The telling is Loeb's later theory that the object is an artificial light sail, which is a separate story about how to interpret it.

candidates.title: 2020 Pan-STARRS object turns out to be a 1966 NASA booster
candidates.quote: In September of 2020, Pan-STARRS found another object that was similarly baffling.

link.reason: The telling is about a different Pan-STARRS object: one found in 2020 that turned out to be a 1966 NASA rocket booster. The nearest story is 'Oumuamua, discovered in 2017, which is a separate object and discovery.

candidates.title: Galileo Project instruments on Harvard College Observatory
candidates.quote: I received thousands of emails from people that are excited to contribute to the project. By now, we have more than a hundred scientists engaged in the Galileo Project. We are purchasing the instrumentation that we will place on the roof of the Harvard College Observatory in the coming months.

link.reason: The telling is about Avi Loeb's Galileo Project putting instruments on the Harvard College Observatory roof. No story here covers the Galileo Project. The nearest one, John Mack's 1990s Harvard abduction study, is a different program from a different decade that just happens to be at the same university.

candidates.title: Fermi's 'Where is everybody?' lunch
candidates.quote: You know, 70 years ago, Enrico Fermi went to lunch with his colleagues, and they talked on the question of how likely it is that there are extraterrestrials out there.

link.reason: Both credit Enrico Fermi with musing about extraterrestrials around 1950, at the Los Alamos lunch that gave rise to the Fermi paradox. Michels's telling, about Fermi thinking about aliens in his off time at Los Alamos, points to the same episode.
link.difference: Loeb sets it at a specific lunch with colleagues about 70 years ago and gives the question discussed (how likely extraterrestrials are), but names no place, where the story places it at Los Alamos without mentioning a lunch.

candidates.title: John Mack's abductee interviews at Harvard
candidates.quote: You have a predecessor at Harvard, a guy named John Mack, who was head of the the psychiatry department, who looked into kind of alien abduction stuff on a more of an anecdotal, kind of personal level.

link.reason: Both tellings are about John Mack, head of Harvard psychiatry, studying alien abductions in the 1990s. That is the same research program at the same grain.

candidates.title: Nolan's brain findings in pilots who see UFOs
candidates.quote: But if we find out that a disproportionate amount of fighter pilots who see UFOs have an enlarged caudate nucleus and putamen.

link.reason: Both tell of Garry Nolan's Stanford brain-imaging finding that people who had UFO encounters show an enlarged caudate nucleus and putamen. The host is retelling Nolan's finding, and Nolan tells it first-hand in the story.
link.difference: The host tells it second-hand and as a hypothetical about fighter pilots who see UFOs being disproportionately affected, where Nolan describes MRIs of DoD and intelligence personnel he was shown.

candidates.title: Metaverse as answer to the Fermi paradox

link.reason: Loeb's theory says the metaverse could explain the Fermi paradox. The nearest stories are Fermi thinking about aliens at Los Alamos in the 1940s and Weinstein's North Sentinel Island analogy, and both are different claims.
